Part II Mechanism
05 / 39
§ 02  ·  What is ARNI?

Sacubitril / Valsartan — a first-in-class dual-acting neurohormonal modulator.

Sacubitril
Neprilysin Inhibitor
  • Blocks degradation of natriuretic peptides (ANP, BNP, CNP)
  • Increases bradykinin levels
→ Natriuresis · Vasodilation · Anti-fibrosis
Valsartan
AT1 Receptor Blocker
  • Blocks angiotensin II at the AT1 receptor
  • Inhibits RAAS over-activation
→ ↓ Aldosterone · Anti-remodeling
Ref: Vardeny O, Miller R, Solomon SD. Combined neprilysin & RAS inhibition for HF. JACC Heart Fail 2014;2(6):663-70 PMID 25306450  ·  McMurray JJV et al. PARADIGM-HF. NEJM 2014;371:993-1004 PMID 25176015.

Part II Cardio-Renal Synergy
06 / 39
§ 02  ·  Foundation of Synergy

Why ARNI protects the kidney.

ComponentTargetPathwayEffect
Sacubitril Neprilysin inhibition ↑ NP (ANP, BNP) · ↑ Bradykinin Natriuresis · Vasodilation · Anti-fibrosis
Valsartan AT1 receptor blockade Inhibits RAAS ↓ Aldosterone · Anti-remodeling
Combined Dual neurohormonal NP enhancement + RAAS suppression Cardio-renal protection
Why this matters for the kidney
  • Natriuretic peptides are endogenous renal protectors.
  • Promote afferent arteriolar vasodilation → ↓ intraglomerular pressure.
  • Combined with efferent vasodilation → dual glomerular protection.
  • Anti-fibrotic effects reduce tubulo-interstitial fibrosis.
Two arterioles, one principle — NP relax the afferent, Valsartan relaxes the efferent; the glomerulus is decompressed from both sides.
Ref: Packer M et al. Circulation 2015;131(1):54-61 PMID 25403646  ·  Damman K et al. Renal effects in PARADIGM-HF. JACC Heart Fail 2018;6(6):489-98 PMID 29655829  ·  Judge P et al. Neprilysin inhibition in CKD. Nephrol Dial Transplant 2015;30(5):738-43 PMID 25140014.

Part II A Lesson in Failure
07 / 39
§ 02  ·  The Concept Born from a Failure

The drug that almost wasn’t.

The pre-history
The natriuretic-peptide system was the obvious next neurohormonal target after RAAS — but for two decades, every attempt to drug it failed. Omapatrilat, a vasopeptidase inhibitor that blocked both ACE and neprilysin, was the late-1990s frontrunner.
OVERTURE (2002) Chronic HF, n=5,770.
Omapatrilat not superior to enalapril.
OCTAVE (2004) Hypertension, n=25,302.
Angioedema 3.0× higher vs. enalapril (2.17% vs 0.68%).
FDA decision 2002 — Refused approval.
Vasopeptidase inhibition abandoned.
The design lesson that gave us ARNI
  • Bradykinin is degraded by both ACE and NEP.
  • Block both → bradykinin accumulates → angioedema risk soars.
  • Solution: pair NEP inhibition with an ARB, not an ACEi — spare ACE so bradykinin still has a clearance pathway.
  • Novartis embodied this in LCZ696 — sacubitril (NEP-i prodrug) co-crystallised 1:1 with valsartan (ARB).
One ACE-inhibitor decision — replaced by an ARB — turned a failed drug class into a Class I therapy.
Ref: Packer M et al. OVERTURE. Circulation 2002;106(8):920-6 PMID 12186794  ·  Kostis JB et al. OCTAVE. Am J Hypertens 2004;17(2):103-11 PMID 14751650  ·  Hubers SA, Brown NJ. Circulation 2016;133(11):1115-24 PMID 26976916.

Part II Proof of Concept

§ 02  ·  The Phase 2 Stepping Stone

PARAMOUNT — the trial that earned two Phase 3s.

Design
TrialPARAMOUNT (Solomon SD et al.)
YearLancet 2012;380:1387-95
Population301 patients · LVEF ≥ 45%
ComparatorLCZ696 vs. valsartan, 36 weeks
PrimaryNT-proBNP change at week 12
ResultPre-specified primary met (p = 0.005)
A small Phase 2 in a preserved-EF population — but the biomarker signal opened the door to both Phase 3 programmes that would define the next decade.
Why PARAMOUNT mattered
  • First clinical confirmation that pairing NEP-i with an ARB was tolerable — no angioedema excess.
  • Provided the regulatory rationale to launch:
    • PARADIGM-HF (HFrEF, LVEF ≤ 40%) → positive 2014
    • PARAGON-HF (LVEF ≥ 45%) → near-miss 2019
  • Established NT-proBNP as a Phase 2 surrogate — still used today (PIONEER, PARAGLIDE, PREMIER).
Ref: Solomon SD et al. PARAMOUNT. Lancet 2012;380(9851):1387-95 PMID 22932717  ·  Eadie AL et al. Pharmacol Res Perspect 2021;9(3):e00794 PMID 34087050.

§ 03  ·  The Field that PARADIGM Created

One trial in 2014 → 2,607 peer-reviewed papers by 2026.

PubMed cumulative
Total publications 2010-2026
2,607
peak year 2022 (386 papers); 2025 still 332.
  • 2014 → 2022: a 12-fold increase in annual output, peaking with the AHA/ACC/HFSA Class I HFrEF guideline.
  • 2024-25: literature shifts from RCTs to real-world cohorts (Swedish nationwide, US Optum) and Asian-specific data (PREMIER, KorAHF, TSOC).
  • Now includes paediatrics (PANORAMA-HF), dialysis (Nguyen 2025 SRMA), MR (PRIME), peripartum CMP, dystrophinopathy — well beyond classic HFrEF.

Why super-responders emerge
01   Young DCMP patients have massive reverse-remodeling potential.

PARADIGM-HF Renal Data
  • ↓ 21% CV death and HFH in CKD patients (eGFR + 0.43 mL/min/yr vs. enalapril).

  • Benign UACR rise reflects mesangial relaxation, not podocyte damage.

§ 08  ·  Daily Practice

2024 ACC ECDP — ARNI is first-line.

2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway
ARNI is the 1st Line
Class I Therapy for HFrEF.
ACEi / ARB — only if ARNI is contraindicated or not tolerated.
Actionable CKD Dosing Guide
eGFRStarting DoseTitrationMonitoring
≥ 3049/51 mg BIDq 2 wks → 97/103 mg BIDStandard
< 30 / Dialysis24/26 mg BIDSlow 2–4 wk titrationK⁺, BP, Cr each step
Titration Algorithm
1Identify eligible HFrEF patient (LVEF ≤ 40%).
2Check eGFR, K⁺, SBP.
├eGFR ≥ 30, K⁺ < 5.2, SBP ≥ 100  →  Standard pathway.
└eGFR < 30 or dialysis  →  Low-dose pathway.
3ACEi washout (36 hours) if applicable.
4Initiate Entresto — 49/51 mg BID standard · 24/26 mg BID low-dose.
5Monitor at 1–2 weeks — BP, K⁺, Cr.
6Up-titrate if tolerated  →  target 97/103 mg BID.
7Follow-up — renal function q 3–6 months.
Ref: 2024 ACC Expert Consensus Decision Pathway (Maddox TM et al.). JACC 2024;83(15):1444-88 PMID 38466244  ·  Heidenreich PA et al. 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA HF Guideline. Circulation 2022;145(18):e895-e1032 PMID 35363499  ·  Entresto® Prescribing Information (Novartis).

Closing Key Takeaways
38 / 39
§ Closing

Five things to remember.

01
A decade of proven excellence.
PARADIGM-HF established ARNI as the gold standard; subsequent trials and RWE have only strengthened the evidence.
02
New evidence confirms broad benefits.
Japan PREMIER, Swedish nationwide (SwedeHF) and US Optum RWE confirm benefit across populations.
03
Consistent benefit across the CKD spectrum.
From normal eGFR to ESKD on dialysis — cardio-renal protection at every stage.
04
De novo HFrEF — start early.
First-line ARNI in de novo HFrEF cuts all-cause hospitalization by 19% (primary); exploratory mortality signal suggests a 30% reduction (Bhatt 2025).
05
Act now — don't wait.
2024 ACC ECDP positions ARNI as 1st line. Early initiation maximizes reverse remodeling — delay is a choice with consequences.
Ref: McMurray NEJM 2014 PMID 25176015  ·  Tanaka Eur Heart J 2024;45(42):4482-93 PMID 39215531  ·  Fu SwedeHF. Clin Res Cardiol 2023;112(1):167-74 PMID 36443599  ·  Bhatt US Optum. Closing Thank You
39 / 39
§ Closing

Ten years. One molecule.
A decade of evidence.

From PARADIGM to the bedside
From a single landmark trial in 2014 to a decade of evidence spanning HFrEF, preserved-EF heart failure, acute decompensation, CKD stage 3b, and dialysis. From North America to Asia. From the failure of Omapatrilat to ARNI as Class I first-line therapy in 2024.
The next ten years
Generic competition will broaden access. The remaining work is to close the prescribing gap — especially in CKD 3b-and-beyond, where evidence is now solid but treatment rates remain only single-digit percent.
Thank you.
Mu-Yang Hsieh, MD, PhD, FESC · NTUH Hsin-Chu Branch · TSOC 2026
